gen-gf-gabarito-fs-bespoke-sans: Gabarito looks drawn with a single nib, its open terminals letting each counter flow outward. Bespoke Sans sits underneath, sharp and refined, with generous gaps where curves meet stems, so the expressive top and the crisp text feel like one voice.
gen-gf-goldman-archivo: Goldman spreads its letters wide, with round forms like open parentheses and a lowercase that nearly matches the capitals. Archivo takes the other job, curving outward in an editorial, approachable way, so Goldman handles the commanding entrance while the text gets the easy reading.
gen-dafont-capture-smallz-switzer: Switzer reads like wire, tubular and Swiss, with a tall waist line and tips that never crowd each other. Give it a little extra size, since Capture Smallz is raw enough already.
gen-dafont-bloody-fs-fira-sans: Bloody pours out big round lowercase bowls, heavy and commanding. Fira Sans, a plain sans with a generous x-height and no thick-thin swing, gives those bowls a steady, uncluttered partner to lean against.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-fs-asap: Wide-spaced, artistic, almost flat in tone. Bushcraft keeps its curves at a single weight and barely lets capitals rise, while Asap, a plain sans, opens its curves into arcs and brings the lowercase nearly up to cap height, giving the pair a shared steadiness.
gen-dafont-conthrax-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads like a loose wire, curvy and approachable with stubby ascender tips. Conthrax stands above it in geometric, wide-mouthed letters where capitals barely outrank the lowercase, so the heading and text feel cut from the same clean, tall-bodied cloth.
gen-dafont-dogica-fs-supreme: Dogica's lowercase climbs nearly to cap height, and its wide tracking lets every curve end stand open. Supreme carries that openness into the text, crisp and dense through the middle of each line, so the heavy heading and the sans body feel built on the same idea.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-general-sans: General Sans reads smoothly, with a tall x-height filling the line and curves that glide without a snag. Edo SZ adds classic, cast-iron weight above it, and its constant stroke keeps company easily with that plain sans text.
gen-dafont-eight-bit-dragon-manrope: Eight Bit Dragon strides across widely spaced, towering lowercase letters, with a gentle shift in stroke weight. And Manrope, a plain sans, keeps one unbroken line from terminal to junction, so it offers the quiet, bright-mouthed reading the heading never tries to give.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-satoshi: Aggressive and fast, Ethnocentric pushes its big bowls apart under short ascenders. Satoshi, a plain sans, counters with a soaring x-height and a wide-open e, and that shared clarity of line is what holds the pair together.
